title: Call interop strictness profiles and error mitigation playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a standardized set of interoperability profiles for function/tool call parameter schemas, a compact error taxonomy, and a runtime mitigation playbook to reduce customer-visible failures during schema evolution and cross-SDK calls. This ticket defines format conventions for our JSON schema surface, runtime validation modes (strict, compatibility, permissive), mapping rules for legacy/third-party payloads, and an actionable error classification with remediation guidance for callers and SDKs.
background: Multiple services and third-party SDKs produce incompatible or slightly off-shape tool call payloads. We currently reject many of these at runtime leading to user-facing errors. Previous tickets implemented localized validators but lack a consistent set of profiles, error codes, or guidance for automatic repair/transform. This work consolidates learnings into a single, versioned spec and runtime implementation plan so rollouts are observable and safe.
proposed_solution: Introduce three validation profiles: 'strict' (full JSON Schema enforcement, used for internal-critical tool calls), 'compatibility' (reject only blocking issues, coerce where safe, emit warnings), and 'permissive' (best-effort acceptance with normalization and audit). Define a compact error code scheme (ERR_MALFORMED_JSON, ERR_MISSING_REQUIRED, ERR_TYPE_MISMATCH, ERR_UNEXPECTED_ENUM, ERR_DEPRECATION, ERR_TRANSFORMATION_FAILED) and attach remediation hints in error payloads. Implement a lightweight 'schema adaptor' layer: a set of declarative transforms (rename, coerce types, fill defaults) that can be applied before validation. Add instrumentation for validation outcomes (acceptance rate, coercions applied, error counts) and an automated canary that starts in permissive mode, ramps compatibility transforms, then flips strict when stability metrics are met.
acceptance_criteria: A v1 spec document describing the JSON schema conventions and the three validation profiles is published to Docs and linked from the SDKs
Runtime supports profile selection per-route/model and logs a structured validation outcome for every call
Compact error codes are returned to callers with human-friendly hints and an optional 'repair' suggestion when applicable
Schema adaptor supports at least three transform primitives: rename, numeric-string coercion, and default-fill, and can be enabled per-field via spec metadata
A canary rollout plan exists and a dashboard shows acceptance rate, transformation rate, and top error types
Unit and integration tests cover representative legacy payloads and confirm no regressions for strict mode after rollout
implementation_tasks: Draft v1 spec: validation profiles, error taxonomy, adaptor metadata syntax
Design schema adaptor DSL and implement core transform primitives (rename, coerce, default, enum-map)
Extend runtime validator to emit structured outcomes and metrics (prometheus + tracing tags)
Add SDK helpers to surface error codes and optional automatic repair steps to callers
Build admin UI hooks in Console to configure profile per-route and toggle adaptor rules
Create test harness with synthetic legacy payloads and edge cases
Prepare canary and rollback automation in deployment pipeline
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Overzealous coercion may silently change intent. Mitigation: require explicit per-field enablement in adaptor metadata and log every coercion as a warning with link to request id
Risk: Performance regression from validation and transforms. Mitigation: benchmark common paths, compile adaptor transforms to bytecode optimized routes, and gate on request size/latency thresholds
Risk: SDK fragmentation if clients ignore error codes. Mitigation: ship SDK helpers that normalize errors and provide repair methods; update docs and release notes
Risk: Security angle where transforms could open injection vectors. Mitigation: include security review and fuzz testing; disallow transforms that change structural nesting or execute code
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Spec + implementation in staging; run self-tests against historical traffic replay
Phase 1: Enable permissive profile by default; collect metrics for 2 weeks
Phase 2: Gradually apply compatibility transforms for high-volume routes with low error rates; monitor transformation acceptance and user impact
Phase 3: For selected internal-only tools flip to strict and verify no new errors; iterate on transforms for public routes
Phase 4: Document final guidance and mark spec v1 stable; schedule follow-ups for v2 to add schema version negotiation
metrics: validation.coercion_rate (number of transforms applied / total calls)
test_plan: Unit tests for adaptor primitives and JSON Schema compliance
Integration tests that replay historical failing payloads and verify acceptance or correct error mapping
Performance benchmark comparing strict vs permissive on representative load
End-to-end canary test with synthetic clients exercising SDK repair helpers
